references.text: Moses is commanded to bring Aaron and his sons forward and wash them with water as part of the consecration of the tabernacle.
Moses carries out the command by bringing Aaron and his sons forward and washing them with water during the priestly ordination ceremony.
Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and feet with water from the bronze basin before serving, to avoid death.
Aaron is to wash his body with water before putting on the holy garments on the Day of Atonement.
The Levites were to be cleansed by sprinkling them with purification water, as a parallel to the washing of the priests.
It speaks of the body being washed with clean water, pointing back to the Old Testament cleansing of the priests.
Jesus washes his disciples' feet and speaks about the necessity of being washed to have a share with him, reflecting the priests' cleansing.
Paul speaks of the washing that regenerates, connecting it to the ritual washing at priestly consecration.
It distinguishes between the initial full washing and the daily maintenance washing, but shares the same theological principle of ritual purity as a prerequisite for service.
